title: You’re not empty… you’re resisting the pouring.
paragraphs: You’re not empty… you’re resisting the pouring.

Because some people are praying for fire…
while quietly protecting the very things God wants to burn.

Before the promise…
there was a confrontation.

Before the outpouring…
there was a tearing.
And most people skip that part.
“I will pour out my Spirit on all flesh…”
But we ignore what came before it.

“Yet even now,” declares the Lord,
“return to me with all your heart,
with fasting, with weeping, and with mourning;
and rend your hearts and not your garments.”

Not your image.
Not your reputation.
Not your Sunday version.

God is not impressed with surface repentance.
He is after the hidden rooms.

Some of us want the Spirit…
but not the surrender.

We want power…
but not purity.

We want to feel God…
but we don’t want to face ourselves.

So we sing louder.
Serve more.
Post verses.

Still hiding.
Still bound.
Still negotiating with sin.
And here’s the tension nobody wants to say out loud:

You cannot be filled with the Spirit
while clutching what grieves Him.
“Do not grieve the Holy Spirit of God…”

That means He is not just power—
He is a Person.
And He refuses to co-exist with what you refuse to surrender.
This is where shame creeps in.

Because now it’s not just about what you’ve done…
it’s about what you’ve been hiding.

The quiet addiction.
The secret compromise.
The pride that masks itself as strength.
The one you hope nobody ever sees.
But here’s the shock of the Gospel:

God already sees it.
And He still calls you back.

To a day when repentance would not just lead to ritual…
but to resurrection life through Jesus Christ.
Because the real problem was never just behavior.

It was sin—
a deep separation between us and God.
And no amount of self-effort can fix that.
So God did what we could never do.

Perfect life.
Sinless heart.
Uncompromised obedience.

“He himself bore our sins in his body on the tree…”
— 1 Peter 2:24

The shame you hide?
He carried it.

The guilt you suppress?
He absorbed it.
So that forgiveness wouldn’t just be declared…

“This is what was spoken by the prophet Joel:
‘In the last days… I will pour out my Spirit on all flesh.’”
The Spirit is not a reward for the perfect.
He is a gift for the repentant.
The same Spirit who fills you…
But He will also confront you.
So if you feel convicted right now…
God is not exposing you to shame you.
He is uncovering you to heal you.
You don’t need to fix yourself first.
He pours on those who turn.

What are you still holding…
that’s keeping you empty?
Say it if you mean it:
And if you know someone who’s silently struggling…
They need truth soaked in grace.
If this stirred something deep in you…
He’s not finished with your story.
Your shame is not the end.
Your hidden life is not beyond redemption.
